title: Establish operational safety budget and automated rollback triggers in PRD after traffic-surge postmortem
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Summary: After the 2025-02-28 traffic-surge incident (large customer onboarding spike) a set of postmortem actions recommended defining an explicit "safe" operational budget per tenant and automated rollback triggers to prevent cascading degradations. This ticket updates the PRD to capture concrete requirements, measurable acceptance criteria, and runbook integration so engineering can implement a runtime safety controller and product can verify via synthetic checks and canary traffic.

Scope: Add PRD sections for (1) operational safety budget definitions (tenant-level budget, global fallback budgets, burn-rate accounting), (2) machine-actionable rollback triggers (signal sources and debounce windows), (3) observability and alerting requirements to support automation, (4) acceptance tests including synthetic scenarios and canary verification, (5) operator UI surface in Console and runtime metrics. Excludes implementation details of kernel selection or quantization changes; those are out of scope and handled in dependent ENG tickets.
background: Incident context: onboarding event produced sustained >10x request rate for a small number of enterprise tenants. Autoscaling stretched pools, queue backpressure increased tail latency, and an aggressive retry loop from a client caused tenant-level burst amplification. Postmortem team recommended: explicit tenant budgets, throttled ingress with graceful degradation, and automated rollback of recent deploys when error-rate and latency correlate with traffic spikes. PM owns translating those actions into product requirements and acceptance criteria that engineering can implement and test.
acceptance_criteria: Safety budget spec published in PRD: per-tenant daily token+request budget, burst window definition, and global emergency budget. Spec must include formulae and example calculations for enterprise and standard tiers.

Automated rollback triggers defined and machine-actionable: clear signal set (5xx rate, p95 latency, queue depth, failed deploy marker), AND/OR evaluation windows (30s/5m), and debounce rules (e.g., 3 consecutive 1m windows breaching thresholds).
Runbook integration points documented: actions for on-call, expected operator notifications, and an option for automatic rollback with human-in-the-loop confirmation for P1 customers.
Observability requirements added: dashboards for per-tenant burn rate, rollback-eligible events, and a synthetic verification dashboard with historical baselines.

End-to-end acceptance tests defined: synthetic canary that simulates tenant spike and verifies rollback trigger executes (or operator workflow) and system recovers to SLO targets within defined SLA time window. Test harness should run in CI on runtime-2.0 branch.
Console UX wireframes for operator view included in PRD with example flows for viewing budgets, marking tenants exempt, and initiating/aborting rollbacks.
Dependencies listed and owners assigned for the engineering tasks required to implement the runtime safety controller and the observability hooks.
tasks: Draft PRD language for safety budget and rollback triggers (PM) — link to PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RES/Safety+Budget+PRD
Collect telemetry spec and thresholds with Observability (PM + Observability Eng) — meeting scheduled 2025-03-14
Define machine-actionable signal contract for ENG (ENG-23487) — owner: runtime-safety team
Design operator Console flows and wireframes (DES) — attach mockups to PRD
Implement synthetic canary tests in CI (ENG-23901) — define scripts and success criteria
Create rollout plan and canary schedule for runtime-2.0 release — coordinate with Release Engineering
Document runbook steps and escalation for on-call (SRE) — include exact playbook commands and expected outcomes
decisions: Decision 1: Safety budgets will be enforced at the edge ingress gate to avoid wasted downstream work (chosen over downstream quota enforcement to minimize wasted GPU cycles).
Decision 2: Automatic rollback is opt-in per-tenant for enterprise customers; default behavior for standard tenants is automated graceful degradation and traffic shaping.
Decision 3: Initial rollback triggers will use conservative thresholds with 3x debounce windows to reduce false positives; thresholds will be tuned after 2 weeks of telemetry.
risks: False-positive rollbacks if thresholds are too sensitive — mitigated by debounce windows and operator confirmation for enterprise tenants.
Incomplete telemetry coverage could make rollback decisions unreliable — dependency on ENG-23487 to deliver consistent signal contract.
Operator fatigue if alerts are noisy — require clear alert routing and aggregated incident buckets in Console.
